subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through the points (3,4), (3,2) and (1,4).

insider_note: Two of the three points share x = 3 and two share y = 4, so each distance equation gives one coordinate of the centre straight away — spotting that saves about half the working.

steps.label: First equation from SA = SB
steps.margin_note: One mark. A and B share x = 3, so the (x₁ − 3)² brackets are identical and cancel before any expansion.
steps.memory_tip: Two points with the same x-coordinate give the centre’s y at once.
lines: Let S(x₁, y₁) be the centre of the circle.
steps.why: A and B differ only in y, so the centre must sit on the horizontal line halfway between them. Cancelling the identical (x₁ − 3)² brackets is what shows that.
common_mistakes: Expanding both (x₁ − 3)² brackets instead of cancelling them.
Taking square roots of (y₁ − 4)² = (y₁ − 2)² and losing the negative case.

steps.label: Second equation from SA = SC
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A and C share y = 4, so this time the y brackets cancel and x₁ falls out.
steps.memory_tip: Same idea turned sideways: two points with the same y give the centre’s x.
steps.why: A and C differ only in x, so the centre sits on the vertical line halfway between them. The y brackets are identical and cancel.
common_mistakes: Squaring out (x₁ − 3)² and (x₁ − 1)² with a sign error on the middle term.

steps.label: Solve for the centre
steps.margin_note: Two marks, even though there is nothing to solve — each equation already gave one coordinate. Write the centre as an ordered pair.
steps.memory_tip: x from (2), y from (1). Read them in the right order: (x₁, y₁) = (2, 3).
steps.why: Each equation isolated a single coordinate, so no simultaneous solving is needed. Only the order of the pair has to be right.
common_mistakes: Writing the centre as (3, 2) by swapping the two results.
Assuming the centre must be one of the given points.

steps.label: Find the radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. r² = 2 here, so r is irrational — keep r² and never write the root.
steps.memory_tip: Keep r squared. The equation of the circle uses r², not r.
lines: A = (3, 4) lies on the circle, so r = SA.
steps.why: The distance from the centre to any of the three given points is the radius. Squaring keeps the number exact instead of leaving a surd.
common_mistakes: Measuring from the wrong point and getting r² = 5.

steps.label: Equation of the circle
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Check the constant: 4 + 9 − 2 = 11.
lines: Circle with centre (2, 3) and r² = 2 is
steps.why: Expanding the centre-radius form gives the general form. The constant term is 4 + 9 − 2 = 11, which is where most of the arithmetic marks are lost.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as (x − 2)² + (y − 3)² = 2 without expanding.
Getting the constant as 13 by forgetting to subtract r² = 2.
